summary: This bill makes state and local law enforcement agencies ineligible for COPS grants unless they enter a 287(g) memorandum of agreement with ICE within 180 days of enactment, starting with fiscal year 2027 applications.

scores.thoughts: The bill conditions eligibility for existing COPS grants on participation in 287(g) agreements but does not alter overall federal spending levels, create new programs, or cut appropriations. It merely reallocates access to already-authorized funds.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to health insurance, providers, or medical services.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The bill directly amends the INA to require state and local law-enforcement agencies to enter 287(g) MOAs with ICE as a prerequisite for COPS grants. This mandates expanded local participation in federal immigration enforcement, clearly advancing border enforcement and restrictionist policy goals.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions involve military or defense appropriations.
No provisions address environmental regulation or climate policy.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or means-tested benefits.
No provisions address schools, school choice, or federal education funding.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement priorities for drugs.

The bill ties local policing grants to immigration enforcement cooperation, indirectly shaping law-enforcement priorities, but its core purpose and text are immigration-specific rather than a general criminal-justice reform measure.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No provisions address deficits, debt ceilings, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address LGBTQ legal protections or related civil-rights measures.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, voter ID, or election administration.
No provisions address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance authorities.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
